blocks.value: A derived class doesn't inherit any constructors from its base class. It needs its own, and the first action inside a derived class constructor is typically to call a constructor from the base class.
A constructor can also call another constructor in the same class using the this keyword:
Here, the default Person() constructor calls the other Person(String) constructor instead of duplicating its logic.

Calling a base class constructor uses super instead, and that call must be the very first action in the constructor. Because of this, a constructor can't use both super and this. If you need both, call this to reach a constructor that itself starts with super.
